report_name: Iran-Linked Hackers Shut Down UK Power Plant in Unprecedented Attack

threat_actors.name: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)
threat_actors.description: A state-sponsored actor linked to Iran's IRGC that conducted a disruptive cyberattack against a UK power generator in July 2026, forcing it offline for four days. The attack is believed to have been a controlled test to demonstrate capability against critical national infrastructure.
threat_actors.goals: Demonstrate capability to disrupt UK critical infrastructure without provoking a major international response.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit Response Function
attack_patterns.description: The threat actors manipulated industrial control systems to shut down a gas-powered generator, preventing its normal safety, protection, or control functions from operating correctly.

tools.name: plink.exe
tools.description: A command-line tool for PuTTY suggested as a potential tool used by threat actors to create SSH tunnels for lateral movement between IT and OT networks.

indicators.name: Plink Tool Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Plink Tunneling Tool Execution
id: 2b8a1f3c-7e4d-4b9a-8f6c-1d2e3f4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of plink.exe, which can be used by adversaries to create SSH tunnels for lateral movement.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-24
references:
  - https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/iran-linked-hackers-blamed-cyber-attack-british-power-plant
tags:
  - attack.t1572
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\plink.exe'
    OriginalFileName: 'plink.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of plink.exe, a command-line tool for PuTTY often used by threat actors to create SSH tunnels for lateral movement.

indicators.name: Windows System Discovery Commands
indicators.pattern:
title: Windows System Discovery Commands
id: 9c8d7e6f-5a4b-4c3d-2b1a-0f9e8d7c6b5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of common Windows discovery commands (net.exe, tasklist.exe, systeminfo.exe) often used by adversaries after gaining initial access.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-24
references:
  - https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/iran-linked-hackers-blamed-cyber-attack-british-power-plant
tags:
  - attack.t1082
  - attack.t1057
  - attack.discovery
level: low
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\net1.exe'
      - '\tasklist.exe'
      - '\systeminfo.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of common Windows discovery commands (`net use`, `tasklist`, `systeminfo`) that adversaries use for reconnaissance after gaining initial access.

indicators.name: Anomalous IT to OT Network Traffic
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous IT to OT Network Traffic
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects potentially unauthorized remote access attempts (RDP, SSH) from an IT network segment to an OT network segment. Subnets are placeholders and must be adapted to the specific environment.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-24
references:
  - https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/iran-linked-hackers-blamed-cyber-attack-british-power-plant
tags:
  - attack.t1021
  - attack.lateral_movement
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    src_ip|cidr:
      - '192.168.1.0/24' # Example IT subnet
      - '10.10.0.0/16'   # Example IT subnet
    dst_ip|cidr:
      - '192.168.100.0/24' # Example OT subnet
    dst_port:
      - 22
      - 3389
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects unusual traffic, such as RDP or SSH, between corporate IT and Operational Technology (OT) networks, which could indicate lateral movement towards control systems.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous IT to OT Network Traffic
